The retrieved Q&A matches suggest that there is some information available on whether a perforated appendix may be associated with an increased risk of tubal infertility and ectopic pregnancy. 

While certain studies have investigated this question, the conclusion drawn from these studies is not definitive. The methodological limitations in those studies mean that their findings cannot be relied upon as conclusive.

To determine if there is sufficient evidence to support a causal relationship between perforated appendix and increased risk of tubal infertility and ectopic pregnancy, additional research is recommended. This would involve conducting well-designed case-control or cohort studies with unbiased ascertainment of exposure (in this case, the perforation of the appendix) and adjustment for confounding variables.

In the absence of such evidence, it can be concluded that the current data do not support a causal relationship between perforated appendix and increased risk of tubal infertility and ectopic pregnancy.
